section_1.title: The Puzzle Setup: Rules of the Game
section_1.content: Introduce the Tower of Hanoi components: three vertical pegs and a stack of 'n' disks of different sizes. Explain the two core rules: 1. Only one disk can be moved at a time. 2. A larger disk can never be placed on top of a smaller disk. Establish the goal: move the entire stack to a different peg in the minimum number of moves.
section_1.example: A curious robot named 'Alpha' is trying to move 3 golden pancakes from Peg A to Peg C without ever squashing a smaller pancake.

section_2.title: Prerequisite: Binary Counting as a Pulse
section_2.content: Visualize binary counting as a sequence of bits flipping. Explain that in a binary number, each position (bit) represents a power of 2. Show a 3-bit counter (000 to 111) and highlight which specific bit changes during each increment. Use a 'lightbulb' graphic where 'Off' is 0 and 'On' is 1.
section_2.example: Sequence: 000 -> 001 (Bit 1 flips) -> 010 (Bit 1 and 2 flip) -> 011 (Bit 1 flips). Notice that Bit 1 flips every 1 step, Bit 2 every 2 steps, and Bit 3 every 4 steps.

section_3.title: The Mapping: Disks as Bits
section_3.content: Create a one-to-one mapping between the binary bits and the disks. Disk 1 (smallest) corresponds to the rightmost bit (2^0). Disk 2 corresponds to the second bit (2^1), and so on. Explain the 'Magic Rule': Whenever a bit in the binary counter changes its value (0 to 1 or 1 to 0), the corresponding disk must be moved.
section_3.example: In a 3-disk game, counting from 0 to 7 in binary (000 to 111) provides the exact timing for every move. When the counter goes from 000 to 001, Bit 1 changes, so we move Disk 1.

section_4.title: The Directional Logic: Where to Move?
section_4.content: Explain the spatial logic using a cyclic movement pattern. For an odd number of disks: move the smallest disk in the cycle A -> C -> B -> A. For an even number: A -> B -> C -> A. All other disks move to the only available legal position. This ensures the binary 'flip' always results in a valid move.
section_4.example: Graphic: A triangular path showing Pegs A, B, and C. When the binary counter hits '001', Disk 1 (the smallest) follows the arrow from A to C.

section_5.title: Synthesis: Solving the 3-Disk Puzzle
section_5.content: Walk through the full 7-step solution ($2^3 - 1$) by incrementing the binary counter. Show a split-screen: left side increments binary (001, 010, 011...), right side animates the corresponding disk move. Emphasize that the 'rightmost changed bit' always identifies the disk to be moved.
section_5.example: At Step 4 (binary 100), the 3rd bit is the rightmost bit that changed from the previous state (011). Therefore, we move Disk 3 (the largest).

section_6.title: Conclusion: The Power of 2^n - 1
section_6.content: Summarize why binary counting is the perfect mathematical model for this recursive problem. Introduce the formula for total moves: $M = 2^n - 1$. Explain that the binary representation of the move number tells you exactly which disk is currently in motion.
section_6.example: If you had 64 disks like the Monks in the original legend, the binary counter would reach a number with 64 ones, taking $2^{64}-1$ moves—roughly 585 billion years!

text_parts:
I have drafted and implemented animation steps for all six sections of the Tower of Hanoi binary solution video. These animations were developed based on the section outlines and examples to maintain progress while the final lecture lines are being finalized.

Key animation features include:
- **Section 1**: Visualizing the setup and the core rules (one disk at a time, no larger on smaller).
- **Section 2**: A 3-bit binary counter and lightbulb toggling to demonstrate the "pulse" of binary counting.
- **Section 3**: Direct mapping of disks to specific bits.
- **Section 4**: Triangular cyclic path logic for disk movement.
- **Section 5**: A split-screen synthesis showing the binary counter and the tower moves in sync for a 3-disk puzzle.
- **Section 6**: Visualization of the $2^n - 1$ formula and the astronomical time required for 64 disks.

All relevant issues (ID 2, 5, 8, 11, 14, 17) have been updated and are now under review.

section_1.title: The Puzzle Setup: Rules of the Game
section_1.content: Introduce the Tower of Hanoi components: three vertical pegs and a stack of 'n' disks of different sizes. Explain the two core rules: 1. Only one disk can be moved at a time. 2. A larger disk can never be placed on top of a smaller disk. Establish the goal: move the entire stack to a different peg in the minimum number of moves.
section_1.example: A curious robot named 'Alpha' is trying to move 3 golden pancakes from Peg A to Peg C without ever squashing a smaller pancake.

section_2.title: Prerequisite: Binary Counting as a Pulse
section_2.content: Visualize binary counting as a sequence of bits flipping. Explain that in a binary number, each position (bit) represents a power of 2. Show a 3-bit counter (000 to 111) and highlight which specific bit changes during each increment. Use a 'lightbulb' graphic where 'Off' is 0 and 'On' is 1.
section_2.example: Sequence: 000 -> 001 (Bit 1 flips) -> 010 (Bit 1 and 2 flip) -> 011 (Bit 1 flips). Notice that Bit 1 flips every 1 step, Bit 2 every 2 steps, and Bit 3 every 4 steps.

section_3.title: The Mapping: Disks as Bits
section_3.content: Create a one-to-one mapping between the binary bits and the disks. Disk 1 (smallest) corresponds to the rightmost bit (2^0). Disk 2 corresponds to the second bit (2^1), and so on. Explain the 'Magic Rule': Whenever a bit in the binary counter changes its value (0 to 1 or 1 to 0), the corresponding disk must be moved.
section_3.example: In a 3-disk game, counting from 0 to 7 in binary (000 to 111) provides the exact timing for every move. When the counter goes from 000 to 001, Bit 1 changes, so we move Disk 1.

section_4.title: The Directional Logic: Where to Move?
section_4.content: Explain the spatial logic using a cyclic movement pattern. For an odd number of disks: move the smallest disk in the cycle A -> C -> B -> A. For an even number: A -> B -> C -> A. All other disks move to the only available legal position. This ensures the binary 'flip' always results in a valid move.
section_4.example: Graphic: A triangular path showing Pegs A, B, and C. When the binary counter hits '001', Disk 1 (the smallest) follows the arrow from A to C.

section_5.title: Synthesis: Solving the 3-Disk Puzzle
section_5.content: Walk through the full 7-step solution ($2^3 - 1$) by incrementing the binary counter. Show a split-screen: left side increments binary (001, 010, 011...), right side animates the corresponding disk move. Emphasize that the 'rightmost changed bit' always identifies the disk to be moved.
section_5.example: At Step 4 (binary 100), the 3rd bit is the rightmost bit that changed from the previous state (011). Therefore, we move Disk 3 (the largest).

section_6.title: Conclusion: The Power of 2^n - 1
section_6.content: Summarize why binary counting is the perfect mathematical model for this recursive problem. Introduce the formula for total moves: $M = 2^n - 1$. Explain that the binary representation of the move number tells you exactly which disk is currently in motion.
section_6.example: If you had 64 disks like the Monks in the original legend, the binary counter would reach a number with 64 ones, taking $2^{64}-1$ moves—roughly 585 billion years!

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Directional Logic: Where to Move?", [
            "Move disks in a consistent cyclic pattern.",
            "Odd total: move the smallest disk A-C-B-A.",
            "Even total: move the smallest disk A-B-C-A."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Draw Pegs A, B, and C in a triangle with clockwise arrows A to C to B.
        peg_a = Text("Peg A", color=WHITE)
        peg_b = Text("Peg B", color=WHITE)
        peg_c = Text("Peg C", color=WHITE)
        
        self.place_at_grid(peg_a, "B3", scale_factor=0.6)
        self.place_at_grid(peg_b, "E5", scale_factor=0.6)
        self.place_at_grid(peg_c, "E2", scale_factor=0.6)
        
        arrow_ac = Arrow(self.grid["B3"], self.grid["E2"], color=WHITE, buff=0.4)
        arrow_cb = Arrow(self.grid["E2"], self.grid["E5"], color=WHITE, buff=0.4)
        arrow_ba = Arrow(self.grid["E5"], self.grid["B3"], color=WHITE, buff=0.4)
        
        self.play(Write(peg_a), Write(peg_b), Write(peg_c))
        self.play(Create(arrow_ac), Create(arrow_cb), Create(arrow_ba))
        self.wait(1)

            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                # Offset to the right half of the screen
                x = 1.5 + j * 0.8
                y = 2.0 - i * 0.8
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])

        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])

        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(COLOR_LINE3)
        )
        
        # Lightbulbs graphic (Off state)
        def create_bulb(color=GRAY):
            bulb_circle = Circle(radius=0.3, color=color, fill_opacity=0.8)
            bulb_base = Rectangle(height=0.15, width=0.2, color=color, fill_opacity=0.8).next_to(bulb_circle, DOWN, buff=0.05)
            return VGroup(bulb_circle, bulb_base)

        bulb3 = create_bulb(GRAY)
        bulb2 = create_bulb(GRAY)
        bulb1 = create_bulb(GRAY)
        
        bulbs_group = VGroup(bulb3, bulb2, bulb1).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.8)
        self.place_in_area(bulbs_group, "E2", "F5")
        
        # Bit labels below bulbs
        l3 = Text("Bit 3", font_size=20, color=WHITE).next_to(bulb3, DOWN, buff=0.2)
        l2 = Text("Bit 2", font_size=20, color=WHITE).next_to(bulb2, DOWN, buff=0.2)
        l1 = Text("Bit 1", font_size=20, color=WHITE).next_to(bulb1, DOWN, buff=0.2)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(bulbs_group), FadeIn(l3), FadeIn(l2), FadeIn(l1))
        
        # Pulsing Sequence: 011(3) -> 100(4) -> 101(5) -> 110(6) -> 111(7) -> 000(0)
        curr_val = 3
        for _ in range(5):
            curr_val = (curr_val + 1) % 8
            b_str = format(curr_val, '03b')

            next_t3 = Text(b_str[0], font_size=60, color=WHITE).move_to(bit3)
            next_t2 = Text(b_str[1], font_size=60, color=WHITE).move_to(bit2)
            next_t1 = Text(b_str[2], font_size=60, color=WHITE).move_to(bit1)
            
            # Bulb colors: COLOR_LINE3 for ON, GRAY for OFF
            target_c3 = COLOR_LINE3 if b_str[0] == '1' else GRAY
            target_c2 = COLOR_LINE3 if b_str[1] == '1' else GRAY
            target_c1 = COLOR_LINE3 if b_str[2] == '1' else GRAY
            
            self.play(
                Transform(bit3, next_t3),
                Transform(bit2, next_t2),
                Transform(bit1, next_t1),
                bulb3.animate.set_color(target_c3),
                bulb2.animate.set_color(target_c2),
                bulb1.animate.set_color(target_c1),
                run_time=0.7
            )
            self.wait(0.1)

        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Synthesis: Solving the 3-Disk Puzzle", [
            "Increment the binary counter to identify each move.",
            "The rightmost bit flip determines which disk moves.",
            "Step four flips the third bit for the largest disk.",
            "Follow the sequence to reach the final state.",
            "Seven moves complete the three-disk puzzle."
        ])

        # Colors
        COLOR_HIGHLIGHT = "#00FFFF"
        COLOR_GOLD = "#FFD700"
        DISK_COLORS = [BLUE_L, GREEN_L, RED_L]

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        counter_label = Text("Binary Counter", font_size=24, color=WHITE)
        self.place_in_area(counter_label, "A1", "A3", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Initial bits "000"
        bit_vals = ["0", "0", "0"]
        bits_group = VGroup(*[Text(b, font_size=40) for b in bit_vals]).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.4)
        self.place_in_area(bits_group, "B1", "B3", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # Towers setup
        towers_label = Text("Towers", font_size=24, color=WHITE)
        self.place_in_area(towers_label, "A4", "A6", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Pegs at Col 2, 4, 6
        peg_a = Line(self.grid["F2"], self.grid["C2"], color=GREY_C, stroke_width=6)
        peg_b = Line(self.grid["F4"], self.grid["C4"], color=GREY_C, stroke_width=6)
        peg_c = Line(self.grid["F6"], self.grid["C6"], color=GREY_C, stroke_width=6)
        base_line = Line(self.grid["F1"], self.grid["F6"], color=GREY_C, stroke_width=8)
        
        # Disks (d1 is smallest, d3 is largest)
        d1 = RoundedRectangle(width=0.7, height=0.3, corner_radius=0.1, fill_opacity=1, color=DISK_COLORS[0])
        d2 = RoundedRectangle(width=1.0, height=0.3, corner_radius=0.1, fill_opacity=1, color=DISK_COLORS[1])
        d3 = RoundedRectangle(width=1.3, height=0.3, corner_radius=0.1, fill_opacity=1, color=DISK_COLORS[2])
        disks = [d1, d2, d3]
        
        # Position disks on Peg A initially
        for i, disk in enumerate(reversed(disks)):
            disk.move_to(peg_a.get_bottom() + UP * (0.15 + i * 0.35))
            
        self.add(counter_label, bits_group, towers_label, peg_a, peg_b, peg_c, base_line, *disks)

        def get_updated_bits(binary_str, highlight_idx=None):

            self.place_in_area(grp, "B1", "B3", scale_factor=1.0)
            return grp

        # Step 2: 010 -> Disk 2 to B
        # Step 3: 011 -> Disk 1 to B
        moves_1_3 = [
            ("001", 0, peg_c, 0.15),
            ("010", 1, peg_b, 0.15),
            ("011", 0, peg_b, 0.5),
        ]
        
        for b_str, d_idx, target_peg, height in moves_1_3:
            new_bits = get_updated_bits(b_str)
            self.play(
                Transform(bits_group, new_bits),
                disks[d_idx].animate.move_to(target_peg.get_bottom() + UP * height),
                run_time=0.8
            )

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.wait(1.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Binary increments from '011' to '100'; highlight the changed 3rd bit in cyan #00FFFF.
        new_bits = get_updated_bits("100", highlight_idx=0)
        
        # Move Disk 3 from Peg A to Peg C (Aligning with final state goal)
        self.play(
            Transform(bits_group, new_bits),
            disks[2].animate.move_to(peg_c.get_bottom() + UP * 0.15),
            run_time=1.2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Sequence through the remaining steps quickly until the counter reaches '111'.

        # Step 6: 110 -> Disk 2 to C
        # Step 7: 111 -> Disk 1 to C
        remaining_moves = [
            ("101", 0, peg_a, 0.15),
            ("110", 1, peg_c, 0.5),
            ("111", 0, peg_c, 0.85),
        ]
        
        for b_str, d_idx, target_peg, height in remaining_moves:
            new_bits = get_updated_bits(b_str)
            self.play(
                Transform(bits_group, new_bits),
                disks[d_idx].animate.move_to(target_peg.get_bottom() + UP * height),
                run_time=0.5
            )

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(YELLOW)

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Synthesis: Solving the 3-Disk Puzzle", [
            "Increment the binary counter to identify each move.",
            "The rightmost bit flip determines which disk moves.",
            "Step four flips the third bit for the largest disk.",
            "Follow the sequence to reach the final state.",
            "Seven moves complete the three-disk puzzle."
        ])

        # Colors
        COLOR_HIGHLIGHT = "#00FFFF"
        COLOR_GOLD = "#FFD700"
        DISK_COLORS = [BLUE, GREEN, RED]

        # Asset Paths
        TOWER_ASSET = "/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/tower.svg"
        DISK_ASSET = "/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/disk.svg"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)

        # Split screen setup
        # Label for Binary Counter
        counter_label = Text("Binary Counter", font_size=24, color=WHITE)
        self.place_in_area(counter_label, "A1", "A3", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Binary representation
        bits_val = "000"
        bits_vg = VGroup(*[Text(char, font_size=40) for char in bits_val]).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.4)
        self.place_in_area(bits_vg, "B1", "B3", scale_factor=1.0)

        # Towers Label and Icon
        towers_label = Text("Towers", font_size=24, color=WHITE)
        tower_icon = SVGMobject(TOWER_ASSET).set_color(WHITE).set_height(0.5)
        tower_group = VGroup(towers_label, tower_icon).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.3)
        self.place_in_area(tower_group, "A4", "A6", scale_factor=0.7)

        # Pegs and Disks setup
        # Use grid columns 4, 5, 6 for pegs A, B, C
        peg_a_x = self.grid["F4"][0]
        peg_b_x = self.grid["F5"][0]
        peg_c_x = self.grid["F6"][0]
        base_y = self.grid["F1"][1]
        top_y = self.grid["C1"][1]

        peg_a = Line([peg_a_x, base_y, 0], [peg_a_x, top_y, 0], color=GREY_C, stroke_width=4)
        peg_b = Line([peg_b_x, base_y, 0], [peg_b_x, top_y, 0], color=GREY_C, stroke_width=4)
        peg_c = Line([peg_c_x, base_y, 0], [peg_c_x, top_y, 0], color=GREY_C, stroke_width=4)
        base_line = Line([peg_a_x - 0.5, base_y, 0], [peg_c_x + 0.5, base_y, 0], color=GREY_C, stroke_width=6)

        # Create Disks using Assets
        d1 = SVGMobject(DISK_ASSET).set_color(DISK_COLORS[0]).set_width(0.6).set_height(0.3)
        d2 = SVGMobject(DISK_ASSET).set_color(DISK_COLORS[1]).set_width(0.9).set_height(0.3)
        d3 = SVGMobject(DISK_ASSET).set_color(DISK_COLORS[2]).set_width(1.2).set_height(0.3)
        disks = [d1, d2, d3]

        # Initial positioning on Peg A (stacked 3 at bottom, 1 at top)
        for i, d in enumerate(reversed(disks)):
            # d is the disk, i is the stack index (0=bottom, 1=middle, 2=top)
            # reversed(disks) gives [d3, d2, d1]
            d.move_to([peg_a_x, base_y + 0.2 + i * 0.35, 0])

        self.add(counter_label, bits_vg, tower_group, peg_a, peg_b, peg_c, base_line, *disks)
        self.wait(1)

        # Animate moves to reach '011'
        # 001: D1 -> C
        # 010: D2 -> B
        # 011: D1 -> B
        moves_1_3 = [
            ("001", 0, peg_c_x, 0.2),
            ("010", 1, peg_b_x, 0.2),
            ("011", 0, peg_b_x, 0.55),
        ]

        for b_str, d_idx, target_x, target_y_offset in moves_1_3:
            new_bits = VGroup(*[Text(char, font_size=40) for char in b_str]).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.4)
            self.place_in_area(new_bits, "B1", "B3", scale_factor=1.0)
            self.play(
                Transform(bits_vg, new_bits),
                disks[d_idx].animate.move_to([target_x, base_y + target_y_offset, 0]),
                run_time=0.6
            )

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)

        # Binary increments from '011' to '100'; highlight the changed 3rd bit in cyan #00FFFF.
        # Step 4: 100. The 3rd bit (index 0) is highlighted.
        new_bits_4 = VGroup(*[Text(char, font_size=40) for char in "100"]).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.4)
        new_bits_4[0].set_color(COLOR_HIGHLIGHT)
        self.place_in_area(new_bits_4, "B1", "B3", scale_factor=1.0)

        # Move Disk 3 from Peg A to Peg C (Target C to ensure stack finishes on C as per storyboard final state)
        self.play(
            Transform(bits_vg, new_bits_4),
            disks[2].animate.move_to([peg_c_x, base_y + 0.2, 0]),
            run_time=1.2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(YELLOW)

        # Sequence through the remaining steps quickly until the counter reaches '111'.
        # Step 5: 101 -> Disk 1 to A
        # Step 6: 110 -> Disk 2 to C
        # Step 7: 111 -> Disk 1 to C
        moves_5_7 = [
            ("101", 0, peg_a_x, 0.2),
            ("110", 1, peg_c_x, 0.55),
            ("111", 0, peg_c_x, 0.9),
        ]

        for b_str, d_idx, target_x, target_y_offset in moves_5_7:
            new_bits = VGroup(*[Text(char, font_size=40) for char in b_str]).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.4)
            self.place_in_area(new_bits, "B1", "B3", scale_factor=1.0)
            self.play(
                Transform(bits_vg, new_bits),
                disks[d_idx].animate.move_to([target_x, base_y + target_y_offset, 0]),
                run_time=0.5
            )

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(YELLOW)

        # All disks are now stacked on Peg C; the screen glows gold #FFD700.
        glow = Rectangle(
            width=self.camera.frame_width, 
            height=self.camera.frame_height, 
            fill_color=COLOR_GOLD, 
            fill_opacity=0.15, 
            stroke_width=0
        )
        self.play(FadeIn(glow))
        self.wait(2)

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Synthesis: Solving the 3-Disk Puzzle", [
            "Increment the binary counter to identify each move.",
            "The rightmost bit flip determines which disk moves.",
            "Step four flips the third bit for the largest disk.",
            "Follow the sequence to reach the final state.",
            "Seven moves complete the three-disk puzzle."
        ])

        # Colors
        COLOR_HIGHLIGHT = "#00FFFF"
        COLOR_GOLD = "#FFD700"
        DISK_COLORS = [BLUE, GREEN, RED]

        # Asset Paths
        TOWER_ASSET = "/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/tower.svg"
        DISK_ASSET = "/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/disk.svg"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)

        # Split screen setup
        # Label for Binary Counter
        counter_label = Text("Binary Counter", font_size=24, color=WHITE)
        self.place_in_area(counter_label, "A1", "A3", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Binary representation
        bits_val = "000"
        bits_vg = VGroup(*[Text(char, font_size=40) for char in bits_val]).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.4)
        self.place_in_area(bits_vg, "B1", "B3", scale_factor=1.0)

        # Towers Label and Icon
        towers_label = Text("Towers", font_size=24, color=WHITE)
        tower_icon = SVGMobject(TOWER_ASSET).set_color(WHITE).set_height(0.5)
        tower_group = VGroup(towers_label, tower_icon).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.3)
        self.place_in_area(tower_group, "A4", "A6", scale_factor=0.7)

        # Pegs and Disks setup
        # Use grid columns 4, 5, 6 for pegs A, B, C
        peg_a_x = self.grid["F4"][0]
        peg_b_x = self.grid["F5"][0]
        peg_c_x = self.grid["F6"][0]
        base_y = self.grid["F1"][1]
        top_y = self.grid["C1"][1]

        peg_a = Line([peg_a_x, base_y, 0], [peg_a_x, top_y, 0], color=GREY_C, stroke_width=4)
        peg_b = Line([peg_b_x, base_y, 0], [peg_b_x, top_y, 0], color=GREY_C, stroke_width=4)
        peg_c = Line([peg_c_x, base_y, 0], [peg_c_x, top_y, 0], color=GREY_C, stroke_width=4)
        base_line = Line([peg_a_x - 0.5, base_y, 0], [peg_c_x + 0.5, base_y, 0], color=GREY_C, stroke_width=6)

        # Create Disks using Assets
        d1 = SVGMobject(DISK_ASSET).set_color(DISK_COLORS[0]).set_width(0.6).set_height(0.3)
        d2 = SVGMobject(DISK_ASSET).set_color(DISK_COLORS[1]).set_width(0.9).set_height(0.3)
        d3 = SVGMobject(DISK_ASSET).set_color(DISK_COLORS[2]).set_width(1.2).set_height(0.3)
        disks = [d1, d2, d3]

        # Initial positioning on Peg A (stacked 3 at bottom, 1 at top)
        for i, d in enumerate(reversed(disks)):
            # d is the disk, i is the stack index (0=bottom, 1=middle, 2=top)
            # reversed(disks) gives [d3, d2, d1]
            d.move_to([peg_a_x, base_y + 0.2 + i * 0.35, 0])

        self.add(counter_label, bits_vg, tower_group, peg_a, peg_b, peg_c, base_line, *disks)
        self.wait(1)

        # Animate moves to reach '011'
        # 001: D1 -> C
        # 010: D2 -> B
        # 011: D1 -> B
        moves_1_3 = [
            ("001", 0, peg_c_x, 0.2),
            ("010", 1, peg_b_x, 0.2),
            ("011", 0, peg_b_x, 0.55),
        ]

        for b_str, d_idx, target_x, target_y_offset in moves_1_3:
            new_bits = VGroup(*[Text(char, font_size=40) for char in b_str]).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.4)
            self.place_in_area(new_bits, "B1", "B3", scale_factor=1.0)
            self.play(
                Transform(bits_vg, new_bits),
                disks[d_idx].animate.move_to([target_x, base_y + target_y_offset, 0]),
                run_time=0.6
            )

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)

        # Binary increments from '011' to '100'; highlight the changed 3rd bit in cyan #00FFFF.
        # Step 4: 100. The 3rd bit (index 0) is highlighted.
        new_bits_4 = VGroup(*[Text(char, font_size=40) for char in "100"]).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.4)
        new_bits_4[0].set_color(COLOR_HIGHLIGHT)
        self.place_in_area(new_bits_4, "B1", "B3", scale_factor=1.0)

        # Move Disk 3 from Peg A to Peg C (Target C to ensure stack finishes on C as per storyboard final state)
        self.play(
            Transform(bits_vg, new_bits_4),
            disks[2].animate.move_to([peg_c_x, base_y + 0.2, 0]),
            run_time=1.2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(YELLOW)

        # Sequence through the remaining steps quickly until the counter reaches '111'.
        # Step 5: 101 -> Disk 1 to A
        # Step 6: 110 -> Disk 2 to C
        # Step 7: 111 -> Disk 1 to C
        moves_5_7 = [
            ("101", 0, peg_a_x, 0.2),
            ("110", 1, peg_c_x, 0.55),
            ("111", 0, peg_c_x, 0.9),
        ]

        for b_str, d_idx, target_x, target_y_offset in moves_5_7:
            new_bits = VGroup(*[Text(char, font_size=40) for char in b_str]).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.4)
            self.place_in_area(new_bits, "B1", "B3", scale_factor=1.0)
            self.play(
                Transform(bits_vg, new_bits),
                disks[d_idx].animate.move_to([target_x, base_y + target_y_offset, 0]),
                run_time=0.5
            )

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(YELLOW)

        # All disks are now stacked on Peg C; the screen glows gold #FFD700.
        glow = Rectangle(
            width=self.camera.frame_width, 
            height=self.camera.frame_height, 
            fill_color=COLOR_GOLD, 
            fill_opacity=0.15, 
            stroke_width=0
        )
        self.play(FadeIn(glow))
        self.wait(2)

section_1.title: The Puzzle Setup: Rules of the Game
section_1.content: Introduce the Tower of Hanoi components: three vertical pegs and a stack of 'n' disks of different sizes. Explain the two core rules: 1. Only one disk can be moved at a time. 2. A larger disk can never be placed on top of a smaller disk. Establish the goal: move the entire stack to a different peg in the minimum number of moves.
section_1.example: A curious robot named 'Alpha' is trying to move 3 golden pancakes from Peg A to Peg C without ever squashing a smaller pancake.

section_2.title: Prerequisite: Binary Counting as a Pulse
section_2.content: Visualize binary counting as a sequence of bits flipping. Explain that in a binary number, each position (bit) represents a power of 2. Show a 3-bit counter (000 to 111) and highlight which specific bit changes during each increment. Use a 'lightbulb' graphic where 'Off' is 0 and 'On' is 1.
section_2.example: Sequence: 000 -> 001 (Bit 1 flips) -> 010 (Bit 1 and 2 flip) -> 011 (Bit 1 flips). Notice that Bit 1 flips every 1 step, Bit 2 every 2 steps, and Bit 3 every 4 steps.

section_3.title: The Mapping: Disks as Bits
section_3.content: Create a one-to-one mapping between the binary bits and the disks. Disk 1 (smallest) corresponds to the rightmost bit (2^0). Disk 2 corresponds to the second bit (2^1), and so on. Explain the 'Magic Rule': Whenever a bit in the binary counter changes its value (0 to 1 or 1 to 0), the corresponding disk must be moved.
section_3.example: In a 3-disk game, counting from 0 to 7 in binary (000 to 111) provides the exact timing for every move. When the counter goes from 000 to 001, Bit 1 changes, so we move Disk 1.

section_4.title: The Directional Logic: Where to Move?
section_4.content: Explain the spatial logic using a cyclic movement pattern. For an odd number of disks: move the smallest disk in the cycle A -> C -> B -> A. For an even number: A -> B -> C -> A. All other disks move to the only available legal position. This ensures the binary 'flip' always results in a valid move.
section_4.example: Graphic: A triangular path showing Pegs A, B, and C. When the binary counter hits '001', Disk 1 (the smallest) follows the arrow from A to C.

section_5.title: Synthesis: Solving the 3-Disk Puzzle
section_5.content: Walk through the full 7-step solution ($2^3 - 1$) by incrementing the binary counter. Show a split-screen: left side increments binary (001, 010, 011...), right side animates the corresponding disk move. Emphasize that the 'rightmost changed bit' always identifies the disk to be moved.
section_5.example: At Step 4 (binary 100), the 3rd bit is the rightmost bit that changed from the previous state (011). Therefore, we move Disk 3 (the largest).

section_6.title: Conclusion: The Power of 2^n - 1
section_6.content: Summarize why binary counting is the perfect mathematical model for this recursive problem. Introduce the formula for total moves: $M = 2^n - 1$. Explain that the binary representation of the move number tells you exactly which disk is currently in motion.
section_6.example: If you had 64 disks like the Monks in the original legend, the binary counter would reach a number with 64 ones, taking $2^{64}-1$ moves—roughly 585 billion years!

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Data from storyboard
        title = "The Puzzle Setup: Rules of the Game"
        lines = [
            "The Tower of Hanoi has three pegs and disks.",
            "Rule one: move only one disk at a time.",
            "Rule two: no larger disk atop a smaller one.",
            "Goal: move the stack to a different peg.",
            "Binary counting reveals the most efficient solution."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # Colors
        COLOR_DISK1 = BLUE_B
        COLOR_DISK2 = GREEN_B
        COLOR_DISK3 = ORANGE
        COLOR_PEG = GRAY_B
        COLOR_HIGHLIGHT = YELLOW
        COLOR_INVALID = "#FF0000"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # "The Tower of Hanoi has three pegs and disks."
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Pegs - using grid points for alignment
        peg_h = 3.2
        peg_a = Rectangle(width=0.1, height=peg_h, fill_opacity=1, color=COLOR_PEG, stroke_width=0)
        peg_b = Rectangle(width=0.1, height=peg_h, fill_opacity=1, color=COLOR_PEG, stroke_width=0)
        peg_c = Rectangle(width=0.1, height=peg_h, fill_opacity=1, color=COLOR_PEG, stroke_width=0)
        
        self.place_at_grid(peg_a, "D1")
        self.place_at_grid(peg_b, "D3")
        self.place_at_grid(peg_c, "D5")
        
        labels = VGroup(
            Text("A", font_size=24),
            Text("B", font_size=24),
            Text("C", font_size=24)
        )
        labels[0].next_to(self.grid["F1"], DOWN, buff=0.1)
        labels[1].next_to(self.grid["F3"], DOWN, buff=0.1)
        labels[2].next_to(self.grid["F5"], DOWN, buff=0.1)

        # Disks
        disk_h = 0.5
        disk3 = RoundedRectangle(corner_radius=0.1, width=1.8, height=disk_h, fill_opacity=1, color=COLOR_DISK3)
        disk2 = RoundedRectangle(corner_radius=0.1, width=1.3, height=disk_h, fill_opacity=1, color=COLOR_DISK2)
        disk1 = RoundedRectangle(corner_radius=0.1, width=0.8, height=disk_h, fill_opacity=1, color=COLOR_DISK1)
        
        # Stack disks on Peg A using grid slots
        self.place_at_grid(disk3, "E1")
        self.place_at_grid(disk2, "D1")
        self.place_at_grid(disk1, "C1")

        self.play(FadeIn(VGroup(peg_a, peg_b, peg_c)), Write(labels), FadeIn(VGroup(disk1, disk2, disk3)))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # "Rule one: move only one disk at a time."
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Animate top disk (Disk 1) moving from Peg A (C1) to Peg B (E3)
        self.play(disk1.animate.move_to(self.grid["B1"]), run_time=0.4)
        self.play(disk1.animate.move_to(self.grid["B3"]), run_time=0.4)
        self.play(disk1.animate.move_to(self.grid["E3"]), run_time=0.4)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # "Rule two: no larger disk atop a smaller one."
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Try to move Disk 2 on top of Disk 1 at Peg B
        self.play(disk2.animate.move_to(self.grid["B1"]), run_time=0.4)
        self.play(disk2.animate.move_to(self.grid["B3"]), run_time=0.4)
        self.play(disk2.animate.move_to(self.grid["D3"]), run_time=0.4)
        
        # Flash Red indicating invalid move
        flash_rect = SurroundingRectangle(disk2, color=COLOR_INVALID, buff=0.1)
        self.play(Create(flash_rect))
        self.play(disk2.animate.set_fill(COLOR_INVALID), run_time=0.2)
        self.play(disk2.animate.set_fill(COLOR_DISK2), run_time=0.2)
        self.play(FadeOut(flash_rect))
        
        # Return Disk 2 to Peg A
        self.play(disk2.animate.move_to(self.grid["B3"]), run_time=0.3)
        self.play(disk2.animate.move_to(self.grid["B1"]), run_time=0.3)
        self.play(disk2.animate.move_to(self.grid["D1"]), run_time=0.4)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # "Goal: move the stack to a different peg."
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Move Disk 2 to Peg C
        self.play(disk2.animate.move_to(self.grid["B1"]), run_time=0.4)
        self.play(disk2.animate.move_to(self.grid["B5"]), run_time=0.4)
        self.play(disk2.animate.move_to(self.grid["E5"]), run_time=0.4)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # "Binary counting reveals the most efficient solution."
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Highlight entire stack on A (Disk 3) and target Peg C
        highlight_a = SurroundingRectangle(VGroup(peg_a, disk3), color=COLOR_HIGHLIGHT, buff=0.2)
        highlight_c = SurroundingRectangle(VGroup(peg_c, disk2), color=COLOR_HIGHLIGHT, buff=0.2)
        
        self.play(Create(highlight_a), Create(highlight_c))
        self.wait(2)
        self.play(FadeOut(highlight_a), FadeOut(highlight_c))
        self.wait(1)

        # Colors for alignment
        COLOR_LINE1 = "#FFFF00" # Yellow

        self.play(FadeIn(p3), FadeIn(p2), FadeIn(p1))
        
        # Transition 001 -> 010, middle bit green

        new_bit1_w2.move_to(bit1)
        self.play(Transform(bit1, new_bit1_w2))

            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(COLOR_LINE3)
        )
        
        # Lightbulbs graphic (Off state)

            bulb_circle = Circle(radius=0.3, color=color, fill_opacity=0.8)
            bulb_base = Rectangle(height=0.15, width=0.2, color=color, fill_opacity=0.8).next_to(bulb_circle, DOWN, buff=0.05)
            return VGroup(bulb_circle, bulb_base)

        bulb3 = create_bulb(GRAY)
        bulb2 = create_bulb(GRAY)
        bulb1 = create_bulb(GRAY)
        
        bulbs_group = VGroup(bulb3, bulb2, bulb1).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.8)

        self.play(FadeIn(bulbs_group), FadeIn(l3), FadeIn(l2), FadeIn(l1))
        
        # Pulsing Sequence: 011(3) -> 100(4) -> 101(5) -> 110(6) -> 111(7) -> 000(0)

        for _ in range(5):
            curr_val = (curr_val + 1) % 8

            self.play(

                bulb2.animate.set_color(target_c2),
                bulb1.animate.set_color(target_c1),
                run_time=0.7
            )

        # Text '585 Billion Years' appears and slowly scales up in white #FFFFFF.
        
        n_display = MathTex("n = 64", color=WHITE)
        # Representing 2^64 - 1
        moves_val = MathTex(r"M = 18,446,744,073,709,551,615", color=WHITE)
        
        self.place_in_area(n_display, 'C2', 'C5', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.place_in_area(moves_val, 'D2', 'D5', scale_factor=0.6)
        
        time_text = Text("585 Billion Years", color="#FFFFFF")
        self.place_in_area(time_text, 'F2', 'F5', scale_factor=1.0)

        self.play(
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            FadeIn(n_display, shift=UP),
            FadeIn(moves_val, shift=UP)
        )
        self.wait(1.5)
        
        # Final dramatic reveal of the time scale
        self.play(
            FadeIn(time_text),
            time_text.animate.scale(1.4),
            run_time=3,
            rate_func=linear
        )
        self.wait(3)

outline.title: The Mapping: Disks as Bits
outline.content: Create a one-to-one mapping between the binary bits and the disks. Disk 1 (smallest) corresponds to the rightmost bit (2^0). Disk 2 corresponds to the second bit (2^1), and so on. Explain the 'Magic Rule': Whenever a bit in the binary counter changes its value (0 to 1 or 1 to 0), the corresponding disk must be moved.
outline.example: In a 3-disk game, counting from 0 to 7 in binary (000 to 111) provides the exact timing for every move. When the counter goes from 000 to 001, Bit 1 changes, so we move Disk 1.

storyboard.title: The Mapping: Disks as Bits
lecture_lines: Map each disk to a specific binary bit.
The smallest disk corresponds to the rightmost bit.
Second disk maps to the second binary bit.
The largest disk maps to the third bit.
Move the disk when its bit changes value.

        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)

            for j, col in enumerate(cols):

                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]

        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

            FadeOut(d1_label, d2_label, d3_label),

        )

        self.play(
            Create(peg_base), Create(pegA), Create(pegB), Create(pegC),
            FadeIn(bit3_val, bit2_val, bit1_val, counter_labels),
            disk3.animate.move_to(self.grid["F2"] + UP*0.2),
            disk2.animate.move_to(self.grid["F2"] + UP*0.6),
            disk1.animate.move_to(self.grid["F2"] + UP*1.0)
        )
        
        # Bit 2^0 flips: 0 -> 1
        new_bit1_val = Text("1", font_size=36, color=MAGENTA).move_to(self.grid["D6"])
        
        self.play(
            Transform(bit1_val, new_bit1_val),
            disk1.animate.set_color(MAGENTA)
        )
        
        # Move Disk 1 to Peg C
        path_points = [
            disk1.get_center(),
            self.grid["C4"], # Midway UP
            self.grid["F6"] + UP*0.2 # Destination
        ]
        self.play(
            disk1.animate.move_to(self.grid["C2"] + UP*2), # Lift
            run_time=0.5
        )
        self.play(
            disk1.animate.move_to(self.grid["C6"] + UP*2), # Shift
            run_time=0.5
        )
        self.play(
            disk1.animate.move_to(self.grid["F6"] + UP*0.2), # Drop
            run_time=0.5
        )
        
        self.wait(2)

Show a 3-bit counter (000 to 111) and highlight which specific bit changes during each increment. Use a 'lightbulb' graphic where 'Off' is 0 and 'On' is 1.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Data from storyboard
        title = "Prerequisite: Binary Counting as a Pulse"
        lines = [
            "Binary counting uses a sequence of flipping bits.",
            "Each bit position represents a power of two.",
            "Observe which bit flips during each increment."
        ]
        
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)
        
        # Colors for alignment
        COLOR_LINE1 = "#FFFF00" # Yellow
        COLOR_LINE2 = "#00FF00" # Green
        COLOR_LINE3 = "#00FFFF" # Cyan/Blue
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Highlight Line 1
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(COLOR_LINE1))
        
        # Initial bits "000" in White
        bit3 = Text("0", font_size=60, color=WHITE)
        bit2 = Text("0", font_size=60, color=WHITE)
        bit1 = Text("0", font_size=60, color=WHITE)
        
        bits_group = VGroup(bit3, bit2, bit1).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.5)
        self.place_in_area(bits_group, "B2", "C5")
        
        self.play(Write(bits_group))
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # Transition 000 -> 001, rightmost bit yellow
        new_bit1_y = Text("1", font_size=60, color=COLOR_LINE1)
        new_bit1_y.move_to(bit1)
        
        self.play(Transform(bit1, new_bit1_y))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Highlight Line 2
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(COLOR_LINE2)
        )
        
        # Labels for powers of 2 (4, 2, 1) in Green
        p3 = Text("2^2", font_size=24, color=COLOR_LINE2)
        p2 = Text("2^1", font_size=24, color=COLOR_LINE2)
        p1 = Text("2^0", font_size=24, color=COLOR_LINE2)
        
        # Position labels above bits
        p3.move_to(bit3.get_top() + UP * 0.6)
        p2.move_to(bit2.get_top() + UP * 0.6)
        p1.move_to(bit1.get_top() + UP * 0.6)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(p3), FadeIn(p2), FadeIn(p1))
        
        # Transition 001 -> 010, middle bit green
        new_bit2_g = Text("1", font_size=60, color=COLOR_LINE2)
        new_bit2_g.move_to(bit2)
        zero_bit1_w = Text("0", font_size=60, color=WHITE)
        zero_bit1_w.move_to(bit1)
        
        self.play(
            Transform(bit2, new_bit2_g),
            Transform(bit1, zero_bit1_w)
        )
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Transition 010 -> 011
        new_bit1_w2 = Text("1", font_size=60, color=WHITE)
        new_bit1_w2.move_to(bit1)
        self.play(Transform(bit1, new_bit1_w2))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Highlight Line 3
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(COLOR_LINE3)
        )
        
        # Lightbulbs graphic (Off state)
        def create_bulb(color=GRAY):
            bulb_circle = Circle(radius=0.3, color=color, fill_opacity=0.8)
            bulb_base = Rectangle(height=0.15, width=0.2, color=color, fill_opacity=0.8).next_to(bulb_circle, DOWN, buff=0.05)
            return VGroup(bulb_circle, bulb_base)

        bulb3 = create_bulb(GRAY)
        bulb2 = create_bulb(GRAY)
        bulb1 = create_bulb(GRAY)
        
        bulbs_group = VGroup(bulb3, bulb2, bulb1).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.8)
        self.place_in_area(bulbs_group, "E2", "F5")
        
        # Bit labels below bulbs
        l3 = Text("Bit 3", font_size=20, color=WHITE).next_to(bulb3, DOWN, buff=0.2)
        l2 = Text("Bit 2", font_size=20, color=WHITE).next_to(bulb2, DOWN, buff=0.2)
        l1 = Text("Bit 1", font_size=20, color=WHITE).next_to(bulb1, DOWN, buff=0.2)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(bulbs_group), FadeIn(l3), FadeIn(l2), FadeIn(l1))
        
        # Pulsing Sequence: 011(3) -> 100(4) -> 101(5) -> 110(6) -> 111(7) -> 000(0)
        curr_val = 3
        for _ in range(5):
            curr_val = (curr_val + 1) % 8
            b_str = format(curr_val, '03b')
            
            # Prepare next bit texts
            next_t3 = Text(b_str[0], font_size=60, color=WHITE).move_to(bit3)
            next_t2 = Text(b_str[1], font_size=60, color=WHITE).move_to(bit2)
            next_t1 = Text(b_str[2], font_size=60, color=WHITE).move_to(bit1)
            
            # Bulb colors: COLOR_LINE3 for ON, GRAY for OFF
            target_c3 = COLOR_LINE3 if b_str[0] == '1' else GRAY
            target_c2 = COLOR_LINE3 if b_str[1] == '1' else GRAY
            target_c1 = COLOR_LINE3 if b_str[2] == '1' else GRAY
            
            self.play(
                Transform(bit3, next_t3),
                Transform(bit2, next_t2),
                Transform(bit1, next_t1),
                bulb3.animate.set_color(target_c3),
                bulb2.animate.set_color(target_c2),
                bulb1.animate.set_color(target_c1),
                run_time=0.7
            )
            self.wait(0.1)

        self.wait(2)

outline.title: Conclusion: The Power of 2^n - 1
outline.content: Summarize why binary counting is the perfect mathematical model for this recursive problem. Introduce the formula for total moves: $M = 2^n - 1$. Explain that the binary representation of the move number tells you exactly which disk is currently in motion.
outline.example: If you had 64 disks like the Monks in the original legend, the binary counter would reach a number with 64 ones, taking $2^{64}-1$ moves—roughly 585 billion years!

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section6Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Initialize the layout with title and lecture lines
        self.setup_layout("Conclusion: The Power of 2^n - 1", [
            "- Binary counting perfectly models the Tower of Hanoi.",
            "- Total moves equal two to the power n minus one.",
            "- Each move is encoded in the binary sequence."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Initial highlight for the concluding statement
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE), run_time=0.5)
        self.wait(1.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Display the formula 'M = 2^n - 1' in large cyan #00FFFF text.
        # This highlights the mathematical takeaway.
        formula = MathTex("M = 2^n - 1", color="#00FFFF")
        self.place_in_area(formula, 'B2', 'B5', scale_factor=1.8)
        
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"),
            Write(formula)
        )
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Demonstrate the magnitude for n = 64 disks.
        # Show n = 64 and the resulting massive number of moves below it.
        # Text '585 Billion Years' appears and slowly scales up in white #FFFFFF.
        
        n_display = MathTex("n = 64", color=WHITE)
        # Representing 2^64 - 1
        moves_val = MathTex(r"M = 18,446,744,073,709,551,615", color=WHITE)
        
        self.place_in_area(n_display, 'C2', 'C5', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.place_in_area(moves_val, 'D2', 'D5', scale_factor=0.6)
        
        time_text = Text("585 Billion Years", color="#FFFFFF")
        self.place_in_area(time_text, 'F2', 'F5', scale_factor=1.0)

        self.play(
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            FadeIn(n_display, shift=UP),
            FadeIn(moves_val, shift=UP)
        )
        self.wait(1.5)
        
        # Final dramatic reveal of the time scale
        self.play(
            FadeIn(time_text),
            time_text.animate.scale(1.4),
            run_time=3,
            rate_func=linear
        )
        self.wait(3)

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Synthesis: Solving the 3-Disk Puzzle", [
            "Increment the binary counter to identify each move.",
            "The rightmost bit flip determines which disk moves.",
            "Step four flips the third bit for the largest disk.",
            "Follow the sequence to reach the final state.",
            "Seven moves complete the three-disk puzzle."
        ])

        # Colors
        COLOR_HIGHLIGHT = "#00FFFF"
        COLOR_GOLD = "#FFD700"
        DISK_COLORS = [BLUE, GREEN, RED]

        # Asset Paths
        TOWER_ASSET = "/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/tower.svg"
        DISK_ASSET = "/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/disk.svg"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)

        # Split screen setup
        # Label for Binary Counter
        counter_label = Text("Binary Counter", font_size=24, color=WHITE)
        self.place_in_area(counter_label, "A1", "A3", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Binary representation
        bits_val = "000"
        bits_vg = VGroup(*[Text(char, font_size=40) for char in bits_val]).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.4)
        self.place_in_area(bits_vg, "B1", "B3", scale_factor=1.0)

        # Towers Label and Icon
        towers_label = Text("Towers", font_size=24, color=WHITE)
        tower_icon = SVGMobject(TOWER_ASSET).set_color(WHITE).set_height(0.5)
        tower_group = VGroup(towers_label, tower_icon).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.3)
        self.place_in_area(tower_group, "A4", "A6", scale_factor=0.7)

        # Pegs and Disks setup
        # Use grid columns 4, 5, 6 for pegs A, B, C
        peg_a_x = self.grid["F4"][0]
        peg_b_x = self.grid["F5"][0]
        peg_c_x = self.grid["F6"][0]
        base_y = self.grid["F1"][1]
        top_y = self.grid["C1"][1]

        peg_a = Line([peg_a_x, base_y, 0], [peg_a_x, top_y, 0], color=GREY_C, stroke_width=4)
        peg_b = Line([peg_b_x, base_y, 0], [peg_b_x, top_y, 0], color=GREY_C, stroke_width=4)
        peg_c = Line([peg_c_x, base_y, 0], [peg_c_x, top_y, 0], color=GREY_C, stroke_width=4)
        base_line = Line([peg_a_x - 0.5, base_y, 0], [peg_c_x + 0.5, base_y, 0], color=GREY_C, stroke_width=6)

        # Create Disks using Assets
        d1 = SVGMobject(DISK_ASSET).set_color(DISK_COLORS[0]).set_width(0.6).set_height(0.3)
        d2 = SVGMobject(DISK_ASSET).set_color(DISK_COLORS[1]).set_width(0.9).set_height(0.3)
        d3 = SVGMobject(DISK_ASSET).set_color(DISK_COLORS[2]).set_width(1.2).set_height(0.3)
        disks = [d1, d2, d3]

        # Initial positioning on Peg A (stacked 3 at bottom, 1 at top)
        for i, d in enumerate(reversed(disks)):
            # d is the disk, i is the stack index (0=bottom, 1=middle, 2=top)
            # reversed(disks) gives [d3, d2, d1]
            d.move_to([peg_a_x, base_y + 0.2 + i * 0.35, 0])

        self.add(counter_label, bits_vg, tower_group, peg_a, peg_b, peg_c, base_line, *disks)
        self.wait(1)

        # Animate moves to reach '011'
        # 001: D1 -> C
        # 010: D2 -> B
        # 011: D1 -> B
        moves_1_3 = [
            ("001", 0, peg_c_x, 0.2),
            ("010", 1, peg_b_x, 0.2),
            ("011", 0, peg_b_x, 0.55),
        ]

        for b_str, d_idx, target_x, target_y_offset in moves_1_3:
            new_bits = VGroup(*[Text(char, font_size=40) for char in b_str]).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.4)
            self.place_in_area(new_bits, "B1", "B3", scale_factor=1.0)
            self.play(
                Transform(bits_vg, new_bits),
                disks[d_idx].animate.move_to([target_x, base_y + target_y_offset, 0]),
                run_time=0.6
            )

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)

        # Binary increments from '011' to '100'; highlight the changed 3rd bit in cyan #00FFFF.
        # Step 4: 100. The 3rd bit (index 0) is highlighted.
        new_bits_4 = VGroup(*[Text(char, font_size=40) for char in "100"]).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.4)
        new_bits_4[0].set_color(COLOR_HIGHLIGHT)
        self.place_in_area(new_bits_4, "B1", "B3", scale_factor=1.0)

        # Move Disk 3 from Peg A to Peg C (Target C to ensure stack finishes on C as per storyboard final state)
        self.play(
            Transform(bits_vg, new_bits_4),
            disks[2].animate.move_to([peg_c_x, base_y + 0.2, 0]),
            run_time=1.2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(YELLOW)

        # Sequence through the remaining steps quickly until the counter reaches '111'.
        # Step 5: 101 -> Disk 1 to A
        # Step 6: 110 -> Disk 2 to C
        # Step 7: 111 -> Disk 1 to C
        moves_5_7 = [
            ("101", 0, peg_a_x, 0.2),
            ("110", 1, peg_c_x, 0.55),
            ("111", 0, peg_c_x, 0.9),
        ]

        for b_str, d_idx, target_x, target_y_offset in moves_5_7:
            new_bits = VGroup(*[Text(char, font_size=40) for char in b_str]).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.4)
            self.place_in_area(new_bits, "B1", "B3", scale_factor=1.0)
            self.play(
                Transform(bits_vg, new_bits),
                disks[d_idx].animate.move_to([target_x, base_y + target_y_offset, 0]),
                run_time=0.5
            )

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(YELLOW)

        # All disks are now stacked on Peg C; the screen glows gold #FFD700.
        glow = Rectangle(
            width=self.camera.frame_width, 
            height=self.camera.frame_height, 
            fill_color=COLOR_GOLD, 
            fill_opacity=0.15, 
            stroke_width=0
        )
        self.play(FadeIn(glow))
        self.wait(2)

outline.title: The Puzzle Setup: Rules of the Game
outline.content: Introduce the Tower of Hanoi components: three vertical pegs and a stack of 'n' disks of different sizes. Explain the two core rules: 1. Only one disk can be moved at a time. 2. A larger disk can never be placed on top of a smaller disk. Establish the goal: move the entire stack to a different peg in the minimum number of moves.
outline.example: A curious robot named 'Alpha' is trying to move 3 golden pancakes from Peg A to Peg C without ever squashing a smaller pancake.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Data from storyboard
        title = "The Puzzle Setup: Rules of the Game"
        lines = [
            "The Tower of Hanoi has three pegs and disks.",
            "Rule one: move only one disk at a time.",
            "Rule two: no larger disk atop a smaller one.",
            "Goal: move the stack to a different peg.",
            "Binary counting reveals the most efficient solution."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # Colors
        COLOR_DISK1 = BLUE_B
        COLOR_DISK2 = GREEN_B
        COLOR_DISK3 = ORANGE
        COLOR_PEG = GRAY_B
        COLOR_HIGHLIGHT = YELLOW
        COLOR_INVALID = "#FF0000"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # "The Tower of Hanoi has three pegs and disks."
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Pegs - using grid points for alignment
        peg_h = 3.2
        peg_a = Rectangle(width=0.1, height=peg_h, fill_opacity=1, color=COLOR_PEG, stroke_width=0)
        peg_b = Rectangle(width=0.1, height=peg_h, fill_opacity=1, color=COLOR_PEG, stroke_width=0)
        peg_c = Rectangle(width=0.1, height=peg_h, fill_opacity=1, color=COLOR_PEG, stroke_width=0)
        
        self.place_at_grid(peg_a, "D1")
        self.place_at_grid(peg_b, "D3")
        self.place_at_grid(peg_c, "D5")
        
        labels = VGroup(
            Text("A", font_size=24),
            Text("B", font_size=24),
            Text("C", font_size=24)
        )
        labels[0].next_to(self.grid["F1"], DOWN, buff=0.1)
        labels[1].next_to(self.grid["F3"], DOWN, buff=0.1)
        labels[2].next_to(self.grid["F5"], DOWN, buff=0.1)

        # Disks
        disk_h = 0.5
        disk3 = RoundedRectangle(corner_radius=0.1, width=1.8, height=disk_h, fill_opacity=1, color=COLOR_DISK3)
        disk2 = RoundedRectangle(corner_radius=0.1, width=1.3, height=disk_h, fill_opacity=1, color=COLOR_DISK2)
        disk1 = RoundedRectangle(corner_radius=0.1, width=0.8, height=disk_h, fill_opacity=1, color=COLOR_DISK1)
        
        # Stack disks on Peg A using grid slots
        self.place_at_grid(disk3, "E1")
        self.place_at_grid(disk2, "D1")
        self.place_at_grid(disk1, "C1")

        self.play(FadeIn(VGroup(peg_a, peg_b, peg_c)), Write(labels), FadeIn(VGroup(disk1, disk2, disk3)))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # "Rule one: move only one disk at a time."
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Animate top disk (Disk 1) moving from Peg A (C1) to Peg B (E3)
        self.play(disk1.animate.move_to(self.grid["B1"]), run_time=0.4)
        self.play(disk1.animate.move_to(self.grid["B3"]), run_time=0.4)
        self.play(disk1.animate.move_to(self.grid["E3"]), run_time=0.4)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # "Rule two: no larger disk atop a smaller one."
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Try to move Disk 2 on top of Disk 1 at Peg B
        self.play(disk2.animate.move_to(self.grid["B1"]), run_time=0.4)
        self.play(disk2.animate.move_to(self.grid["B3"]), run_time=0.4)
        self.play(disk2.animate.move_to(self.grid["D3"]), run_time=0.4)
        
        # Flash Red indicating invalid move
        flash_rect = SurroundingRectangle(disk2, color=COLOR_INVALID, buff=0.1)
        self.play(Create(flash_rect))
        self.play(disk2.animate.set_fill(COLOR_INVALID), run_time=0.2)
        self.play(disk2.animate.set_fill(COLOR_DISK2), run_time=0.2)
        self.play(FadeOut(flash_rect))
        
        # Return Disk 2 to Peg A
        self.play(disk2.animate.move_to(self.grid["B3"]), run_time=0.3)
        self.play(disk2.animate.move_to(self.grid["B1"]), run_time=0.3)
        self.play(disk2.animate.move_to(self.grid["D1"]), run_time=0.4)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # "Goal: move the stack to a different peg."
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Move Disk 2 to Peg C
        self.play(disk2.animate.move_to(self.grid["B1"]), run_time=0.4)
        self.play(disk2.animate.move_to(self.grid["B5"]), run_time=0.4)
        self.play(disk2.animate.move_to(self.grid["E5"]), run_time=0.4)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # "Binary counting reveals the most efficient solution."
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Highlight entire stack on A (Disk 3) and target Peg C
        highlight_a = SurroundingRectangle(VGroup(peg_a, disk3), color=COLOR_HIGHLIGHT, buff=0.2)
        highlight_c = SurroundingRectangle(VGroup(peg_c, disk2), color=COLOR_HIGHLIGHT, buff=0.2)
        
        self.play(Create(highlight_a), Create(highlight_c))
        self.wait(2)
        self.play(FadeOut(highlight_a), FadeOut(highlight_c))
        self.wait(1)
